findings.title: AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) Vulnerability (AMD-SB-3059)
findings.summary_md: AMD's advisory for Mior (CVE-2026-0462, CVSS 4.0 5.9) describes insufficient granularity of access control in SEV firmware that lets a malicious hypervisor redirect MMIO access and compromise SEV-SNP guest memory integrity. Affected products are five EPYC server lines (7003, 8004, 8005, 9004, 9005) with SEV firmware mitigation dated 2026-08-12 and platform initialization firmware targeted for December 2026, with embedded models in February 2027. Only SEV-SNP is affected, not SEV or SEV-ES, and the advisory lists TCB values for SNP attestation next to each fixed firmware version. Revision dated 2026-11-10.

findings.title: AMD SEV Incomplete Cleanup Vulnerability (AMD-SB-3061)
findings.summary_md: AMD's advisory for Skyfall's VM leak (CVE-2026-40671, CVSS 4.0 4.9) covers incomplete cleanup during VMRUN error handling that can expose SEV-SNP guest register state to a privileged attacker via a Transient Scheduler Attacks side channel. Five EPYC server lines (7003, 8004, 8005, 9004, 9005) receive microcode dated 2026-08-12 and platform initialization firmware targeted for November 2026; the Instinct MI300A receives a patch dated 2026-09-21. Embedded EPYC fixes are targeted between January and April 2027. Revision dated 2026-11-10.

findings.title: EDK II Mitigations for Transient Scheduler Attacks (TSA) (AMD-SB-7072)
findings.summary_md: AMD's EDK II bulletin for Skyfall's SMM leak (CVE-2026-18448, CVSS 4.0 5.6, assigned by the EDK II project) traces the issue to missing TSA mitigations in EDK II firmware that let a ring-0 attacker infer residual microarchitectural state left by SMM. AMD recommends applying previously published TSA mitigations (AMD-SB-7029) plus an EDK II or platform firmware patch targeted for November 2026 on EPYC server lines; platform firmware is already available for EPYC 4004 and 4005. The EDK II project lists no patched version as of the advisory. Revision dated 2026-11-10.

findings.title: Mior: Breaking AMD SEV-SNP with Device-as-Memory
findings.summary_md: The ETH Zurich researchers' page and paper (ACM CCS 2026) detail Mior, reported to AMD on 2026-02-12 with an embargo ending 2026-11-10. The attack redirects PSP initialization writes to attacker-controlled device memory, leaving RMP entries uninitialized so a malicious hypervisor can read or modify confidential VM memory and forge attestation reports. Tested on AMD EPYC 9135 (Zen 5); Zen 3 and Zen 4 considered potentially affected. Requires hypervisor and BIOS/UEFI control plus a PCIe device. PDF last modified 2026-11-10.

findings.title: SKYFALL: Microarchitectural Data Sampling on AMD
findings.summary_md: The ETH Zurich and Google team's page (IEEE S&P 2027) describes Skyfall, a microarchitectural data-sampling attack on AMD processors that builds on Transient Scheduler Attacks (first disclosed 2025-07-08). It recovers SEV-SNP guest register state and disk-encryption keys via aborting VMRUN, reads three fixed cache lines per targeted page, and leaks decrypted microcode and SMM state. Tested on EPYC 7313 (Zen 3) and EPYC 9124/9334 (Zen 4); not shown on Zen 5. AMD assigned CVE-2026-40671 and released microcode updates; EDK II assigned CVE-2026-18448. Page last modified 2026-11-10.
